To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of a paired serum hCG measurement to a single measurement in the early first trimester did not significantly improve the predictive accuracy for miscarriage and live birth in in vitro fertilisation pregnancies.
paired serum hCG measurements are better than a single measurement at predicting the outcome of in vitro pregnancy and that this difference is greatest when the hCG levels are low.

(1) the addition of paired serum hCG measurements to a clinical prediction rule (the ‘2-Step’ rule) did not improve the prediction of pregnancy outcome in women undergoing IVF; and (2) the ‘2-Step Rule’ is a useful and practical tool for predicting the likelihood of miscarriage in women with an IVF pregnancy.

the development of new methods for predicting the success of in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single serum hCG value in the range 25–150 IU/L on the day of the first ultrasound scan (day 21 of gestation) is associated with a good prognosis for a successful pregnancy outcome.

a single serum hCG level is sufficient for the diagnosis of a viable pregnancy in the first 10–14 days of gestation, and that the value of paired measurements in the prediction of pregnancy outcome has not been demonstrated.
the value of a single or paired serum hCG measurement in early pregnancy in predicting the outcome of an IVF pregnancy is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found no difference between the two methods of prediction.
the paired serum hCG measurement in early pregnancy is not more effective in predicting the outcome of an in vitro fertilization pregnancy than a single measurement.
paired measurements are not better than single measurements in the early pregnancy period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of hCG in early pregnancy is not a reliable predictor of the success of an IVF pregnancy.
the use of paired hCG measurements to predict miscarriage in the setting of an in vitro fertilization pregnancy may not be necessary, and that a single hCG measurement may suffice.
the use of hCG doubling time in the early pregnancy period is not a good predictor of pregnancy outcome in IVF patients.
